title: Deferred cleanup (setTimeout in effect cleanup) outlives its session — expose it via a ref and drain synchronously at the next effect run
trigger: An effect cleanup defers DOM/style teardown behind a setTimeout (e.g. exit animation window). If a new effect run starts before the timer fires, the stale restore executes mid-session: it strips the new run's overrides, re-parents shared nodes out of the new tree, and nulls refs the new run just set — plus the new run's 'original state' snapshot captures the old session's overrides.
principle: A cleanup's setTimeout is NOT cancelled by React when the effect re-runs — it fires in whatever world exists at fire time. Fix: store the restore closure in a ref at cleanup time; at the START of the next effect run, drain it synchronously (old session fully torn down → new run snapshots pristine state and builds on a clean tree); guard the restore with a done-flag so the pending timer becomes a no-op. Never let two sessions' restore windows overlap.

cases.context: Split View close schedules a 410ms setTimeout that restores playerShell inline styles + moves #Tihoka-subtitle-root back + nulls splitViewWrapperRef + clears portal target. Reopen <410ms: the old timer fires mid-new-session → removeProperty strips the fresh width/height:100%!important (playerShell collapses inside the new stageTihoka), TihokaRoot leaves the new stage, portal target nulled → CueList unmounts; the new run's savedStyles snapshot had captured the still-active overrides → on final close the overrides persist permanently. Rapid ×10 toggles crashed the page entirely.
A pending fullscreen-settle callback (waitForPlayerSettle → setState(true)) reopens the panel after the user explicitly closed it inside the settle window.
cases.bad:
// settle cleanup only cancelled on unmount
manualToggle = () => setSplitViewOpen(!open);

applyFor: Effect cleanups that defer teardown behind animation/transition windows (slide-out, fade-out) while re-entry is possible
Any setTimeout/rAF scheduled inside a cleanup that mutates shared DOM, refs, or portal targets
Async settle/poll callbacks that setState — always provide a manual-cancel path so user intent wins over pending automation
